speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given the onset of inappropriate behavior, craving sweets, and significant weight gain over six months, have you noticed excessive thirst, frequent urination, or any vision changes? REQUEST TEST: Fasting Plasma Glucose, HbA1c, Basic Metabolic Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inappropriate behavior. I also have Disinterest in family interactions, Craving for specific foods, Significant weight gain, Apathy, Blunted affect. speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of new-onset inappropriate behavior (disinhibition), specific food cravings, apathy, and rapid weight gain is highly suggestive of frontal lobe pathology or a specific metabolic disorder affecting the hypothalamus and frontal cortex. Given the patient's age and the specific nature of the behavioral changes alongside the craving for high-calorie foods, I need to rule out a mass lesion or specific hormonal imbalance before confirming a diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: If MRI is not immediately available, I will proceed with a Thyroid Panel (TSH, Free T4) to evaluate for severe hypothyroidism, though the behavioral changes strongly point toward a structural lesion in the frontal lobe or hypothalamic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your glucose and thyroid panels are normal, and the MRI brain will be critical to rule out a frontal lobe tumor or lesion, please wait a moment while I review those imaging results to confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Frontal Lobe Tumor (e.g., Glioma) or Hypothalamic Pathology causing Disinhibition Syndrome.
